title: Digit Products
statementMd:
## Problem Statement

For how many positive integers at most $N$ is the product of the digits at most $K$?

## Constraints

- $1 \leq N \leq 10^{18}$
- $1 \leq K \leq 10^9$
- All values in input are integers.

## Input

Input is given from Standard Input in the following format:

```
N K
```

## Output

Print the number of integers satisfying the condition.

samples.note: Out of the positive integers at most $13$, there are five such that the product of the digits is at most $2$: $1$, $2$, $10$, $11$, and $12$.
Out of the positive integers at most $100$, all but $99$ satisfy the condition.
Note that the answer may not fit into a $32$-bit integer.
